question: Why is the community health planning cycle described as continuous and circular?

options.A: The exact same health problem must be treated over and over again
options.B: Evaluation findings lead directly into the next round of assessment and planning
options.C: It must be repeated every thirty days regardless of community needs
options.D: Healthcare workers rotate through different villages in a fixed circle

explanation: Because health needs change and programs must adapt, the end of one evaluation simply sparks the beginning of the next planning phase. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the correct nursing action immediately after a patient passes away?

options.A: Leave all hospital equipment and invasive IV lines attached to the body
options.B: Handle the body respectfully and allow family time for viewing
options.C: Call the local media to report the passing of the patient
options.D: Remove all personal jewelry and immediately send it to the pharmacy

explanation: Post-mortem care is all about dignity. Give the family a quiet, respectful moment to see their loved one. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h6)

question: How do drug name stems help a student nurse understand unfamiliar medications?

options.A: They show the exact expiration date and proper storage temperature needed
options.B: They tell the nurse the exact retail price of the medication in the pharmacy
options.C: Common suffixes reveal the pharmacological class and general action of the drug
options.D: They indicate which manufacturing company produced the specific batch of pills

explanation: Drug stems (like '-olol' for beta-blockers) are like cheat codes! They tell you what family a drug belongs to, helping you guess its action even if you've never seen it before. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the ultimate, primary benefit of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written exams and classroom lectures
options.B: Making sure nursing students never have to go to a real hospital
options.C: Improving patient safety and reducing medical errors in hospitals
options.D: Reducing the cost of running nursing schools and hiring staff

explanation: Every simulation exercise is ultimately aimed at protecting real patients by ensuring nurses are well-trained and competent. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is a key administrative duty for a nursing unit manager?

options.A: Designing new blueprints for hospital buildings
options.B: Serving as the legal defense attorney for the hospital
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for the pharmacy
options.D: Conducting regular performance appraisals for ward staff

explanation: Great job! Doing performance reviews helps managers guide their team members, support their growth, and keep ward standards high. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that someone has hyperthyroidism?

options.A: SlOWed heart rate and sluggish mentation
options.B: Intolerance to cold room temperatures
options.C: Severe constipation and dry coarse skin
options.D: Weight loss despite an increased appetite

explanation: Hyperthyroidism puts the body's engine into overdrive! Patients burn through calories so fast that they lose weight even though they are eating way more food than usual. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why should you tell a patient to avoid clearing their throat aggressively right after a laryngoscopy?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from writing the final discharge summary.
options.B: It increases the patient's blood pressure and heart rate significantly.
options.C: It forces the residual topical spray down into the stomach too fast.
options.D: It can cause trauma or irritation to the recently numbed vocal cords.

explanation: Spot on! Since the vocal cords are still a bit sleepy and vulnerable, harsh throat clearing can easily bruise or injure them. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why might a patient having a severe gout flare still show a completely normal blood uric acid level on a lab test?

options.A: Blood tests are completely useless for diagnosing joint pain
options.B: Uric acid only travels through the urine, not the bloodstream
options.C: Blood tests cannot detect uric acid when a person is in pain
options.D: Uric acid can temporarily drop during an acute inflammation flare

explanation: Brilliant! During an actual flare, uric acid levels in the blood can dip down to normal ranges, meaning a blood test alone can sometimes play tricks on you. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h5)

question: A study tests a stress-relief program for nurses in a busy city hospital. What is a great recommendation for future research?

options.A: Firing all city hospital nurses who reported high stress levels
options.B: Replacing human nurses with automated computer terminals
options.C: Testing if the same program works effectively in rural clinics
options.D: Stopping all future research on nurse mental health

explanation: Brilliant! Testing the same idea in a different setting helps us see if it works for nurses everywhere, not just in the city. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why can it be so tricky to spot a drug side effect in someone with a degenerative disease?

options.A: Patients with degenerative illnesses never tell anyone how they feel
options.B: Lab tests can never detect drug levels in chronic illnesses
options.C: Drug side effects always cause a sudden skin rash
options.D: Side effects like tremors or confusion can easily look like the disease getting worse

explanation: You're doing great! It's a classic clinical puzzle: if a drug causes shakiness or confusion, it's easy to assume the disease is simply progressing, when the patient might actually just need a medication adjustment. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h6)

question: Why do safety frameworks focus on system design instead of just blaming the nurse?

options.A: Human error is often triggered by poor processes and workplace design
options.B: Blaming workers is illegal under international labor laws
options.C: Workers never make mistakes if they receive basic orientation
options.D: Systems are easier to replace than trained clinical personnel

explanation: Even great nurses make mistakes when processes are confusing or the ward is chaotic. Fixing the system stops errors before they start! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common mental health challenge for survivors of ongoing abuse?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Well done! Survivors often deal with lasting emotional impacts like anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h3)

question: In the nursing process, what is the evaluation step used to find out?

options.A: Which nurse gets assigned to night shift duty
options.B: Whether patient goals and outcomes have been met
options.C: How much the patient's hospital bill will cost
options.D: What medications the doctor should prescribe next

explanation: Evaluation is your final check in the nursing process to see if your care plan actually helped the patient reach their health goals. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of choosing whole fruit over fruit juice?

options.A: Encouraging healthy chewing and saliva flow
options.B: Providing a concentrated dose of liquid sugar
options.C: Promoting a feeling of fullness after eating
options.D: Supplying beneficial dietary fiber

explanation: You nailed it! Concentrated liquid sugar is actually found in juices, and it can cause your blood sugar to spike quickly. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h4)

question: Why does dead heart muscle (necrosis) increase the risk of the heart wall tearing open?

options.A: Dead tissue instantly turns into hard bone
options.B: Dead muscle tissue loses its strength and tears easily under pressure
options.C: Dead cells make the heart grow too fast
options.D: Blood pressure inside the heart drops to zero

explanation: When heart muscle dies during a heart attack, it turns into a soft, weak spot. Just like a worn-out bicycle tire, that weak spot can blow out under normal pumping pressure. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why must a researcher carefully explain how they chose their participants (sample selection)?

options.A: To make the research budget look much smaller than it is
options.B: To hide the identities of the nurses working on the ward
options.C: So others understand who was studied and can judge if results are fair
options.D: To ensure that only wealthy patients take part in the study

explanation: Being transparent about your participants builds trust and shows everyone that your results are reliable and unbiased. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why do we wait to find out the exact name of the poison instead of panicking right away?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always inaccurate in the first hour
options.B: Immediate life threats must be managed to prevent death
options.C: Hospital policy forbids asking family members about pill bottles
options.D: The poison usually breaks down and cannot be identified later

explanation: Spot on! If a patient's airway is blocked or their heart stops, knowing the chemical name of the poison won't save them. We stabilize life first, investigate second. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h1)

question: If a patient taking a thioamide medication reports which symptom, should you suspect a serious blood issue like agranulocytosis?

options.A: Slight tremors in fingers
options.B: Mild nausea after meals
options.C: Fever and sore throat
options.D: Dry skin and constipation

explanation: Always take a new fever and sore throat seriously with these meds; it can be an early warning sign of a dangerously low white blood cell count. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h7)

question: A patient at a local clinic says they want to stop their modern epilepsy drugs and use unverified traditional herbs instead. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain the risks of stopping medication abruptly and discuss how to safely manage the condition together
options.B: Threaten to report the patient to local authorities if they miss a single clinic appointment
options.C: Advise the patient to stop the medication immediately to see what happens
options.D: Tell the patient that traditional remedies are completely harmless and can replace drugs

explanation: Always meet patients with empathy and respect. Instead of judging, gently educate them on why stopping their meds is dangerous while working together to support their overall health journey. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h8)

question: Why is checking the patient's blood creatinine level so important before an IVP?

options.A: To measure the concentration of red blood cells circulating in the plasma
options.B: To check if the patient has an active bacterial urinary infection
options.C: To calculate the exact amount of oral pain medication the patient needs
options.D: To ensure the kidneys can safely filter out the injected contrast dye

explanation: Creatinine tells us how well the kidneys are working. If they are struggling, the dye could make things worse, so we always check first! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T16#GNS221_U2_T16_h3)

question: Which specific area of the body does a colonoscopy examine?

options.A: The large intestine and rectum
options.B: The upper esophagus and stomach
options.C: The trachea and lower bronchial tubes
options.D: The urinary bladder and urethra

explanation: A colonoscopy is specifically designed to inspect the lining of the large bowel and the rectum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a negative feedback loop?

options.A: Regulating body temperature through sweating
options.B: Releasing oxytocin during childbirth contractions
options.C: Rapidly nursing an infant to increase milk flow
options.D: Forming a hard blood clot over a skin wound

explanation: Sweating is a classic negative feedback response. When you get too hot, your body works to cool you down, bringing things back to normal! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: How does good delegation by a nurse leader show empowerment?

options.A: By shifting unwanted administrative paperwork onto junior staff
options.B: By showing trust in the team's ability to handle important clinical tasks
options.C: By forcing staff to work longer shifts without extra pay
options.D: By removing all accountability from the bedside nurse

explanation: When a leader delegates well, they are saying, 'I trust your skills.' It helps junior nurses grow and take ownership of their duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which clinical situation typically requires the administration of emergency and critical care drugs?

options.A: Discharge planning for a patient with a healed fracture
options.B: Annual physical checkup in a healthy adult client
options.C: A sudden, life-threatening crisis like cardiac arrest
options.D: Routine outpatient follow-up for chronic mild headache

explanation: Emergency drugs are reserved for critical, unstable situations where rapid intervention is necessary to save a life. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main cause of Maternal Depletion Syndrome?

options.A: Repeated, closely spaced pregnancies without adequate recovery time
options.B: A sudden genetic mutation triggered by multiple childbirths
options.C: Exposure to harsh environmental toxins during early adulthood
options.D: Consuming a diet high in processed foods during lactation

explanation: Maternal depletion happens when a mother's body doesn't get enough breathing room to heal and rebuild its nutrient stores between pregnancies. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T8#GNS225_U6_T8_h4)

question: Which glove material gives you a great feel (tactile sensitivity) but can cause nasty allergies?

options.A: Nitrile
options.B: Neoprene
options.C: Vinyl
options.D: Latex

explanation: Natural rubber latex fits like a second skin, but protein allergies make it a risk for both healthcare workers and patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.A: Immunization, Environment, and Community
options.B: Information, Education, and Communication
options.C: Infection Eradication and Control
options.D: Illness Evaluation and Clinical care

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are the foundational pillars of public health messaging and community health promotion. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the best needle size for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 25 to 27 gauge, 1/4 to 1/2 inch long
options.B: 21 to 23 gauge, 1 inch long
options.C: 30 to 32 gauge, 2 inches long
options.D: 18 to 20 gauge, 1 to 1.5 inches long

explanation: You're getting the hang of this! A fine, short needle ensures the medicine stays shallow in the dermis rather than slipping into the fat below. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T8#GNS125_U3_T8_h3)

question: How do clinical audits and incident reports help nursing management?

options.A: By ensuring that nurses never experience stress during their shifts
options.B: By replacing the need for formal hospital administrative authority
options.C: By automatically transferring legal liability to the hospital board
options.D: By providing control mechanisms to monitor performance and correct standard deviations

explanation: Audits and incident reports act as safety nets. They help managers spot mistakes early, track quality, and keep patient care standards high. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h6)

question: A patient with long-term chronic gastritis is most at risk for lacking which vitamin?

options.A: Vitamin C deficiency
options.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency
options.C: Calcium deficiency
options.D: Potassium deficiency

explanation: Exactly! When gastritis damages the stomach's parietal cells, you lose intrinsic factor, meaning your body can't absorb vitamin B12 like it should. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h2)

question: What physical sign is tested by tapping the facial nerve near the cheek to check for low calcium?

options.A: Trousseau's sign
options.B: Brudzinski's sign
options.C: Chvostek's sign
options.D: Homans' sign

explanation: A quick tap on the facial nerve causing the cheek or lip to twitch is a classic positive Chvostek's sign, pointing to low calcium! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why should the nurse advise a patient to bring sunglasses to their ophthalmoscopy appointment?

options.A: Bright sunlight blocks the dilating drops from working properly
options.B: Dilated pupils let in excess light, causing glare and discomfort outdoors
options.C: Sunglasses protect the delicate contact lenses from blowing dust outside
options.D: The bright examination room light permanently damages unshielded eyes

explanation: Because dilating drops keep the pupil wide open, natural sunlight becomes overwhelmingly bright and uncomfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which test is commonly used to screen for too much adrenaline breakdown in a suspected pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Morning serum cortisol levels
options.B: Serum fasting blood glucose
options.C: 24-hour urinary metanephrines
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: Collecting urine over 24 hours lets us measure metanephrines, which are the leftover waste products of extra adrenaline and noradrenaline over a full day. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h6)

question: A patient cries out with sharp, shooting pain down their leg while receiving an IM injection in the buttocks. What has most likely happened?

options.A: The needle has irritated or hit the sciatic nerve
options.B: The muscle is experiencing a normal cramp
options.C: The needle gauge is too small for the fluid
options.D: The medication is reacting with subcutaneous fat

explanation: Shooting pain down the leg is a classic sign of nerve trauma, specifically involving the sciatic nerve during poor dorsogluteal injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of severe cholera infection?

options.A: Rapid dehydration from severe watery diarrhea
options.B: Chronic dry cough and chest pain
options.C: Painful joint swelling and skin rashes
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eyes only

explanation: The bacterium behind cholera produces a toxin that causes massive fluid loss, leading to dangerous dehydration within hours. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical socioeconomic benefit of family planning for a household?

options.A: Increased ability to afford nutritious food and clothing
options.B: Higher likelihood of children completing their education
options.C: Reduced spending on emergency medical care for sick infants
options.D: Guaranteed employment for all children upon reaching adulthood

explanation: Family planning improves financial management and education access, but it does not automatically guarantee employment for children later in life. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h3)

question: Using the Plate Method for diabetes management, what should fill half of the dinner plate?

options.A: Full-fat dairy products
options.B: Starchy grains and yams
options.C: Lean protein foods
options.D: Non-starchy vegetables

explanation: Half of the plate should contain non-starchy vegetables to provide volume and fiber without raising blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h4)

question: What does 'mesial temporal sclerosis' mean in temporal lobe epilepsy?

options.A: Scarring and neuron loss in the hippocampus
options.B: A sudden blockage of the carotid artery
options.C: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain
options.D: Inflammation of the outer brain lining

explanation: Think of mesial temporal sclerosis as scarring deep inside the temporal area (the hippocampus). This damage makes it easier for abnormal electrical storms to start. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h1)

question: What should a nurse expect to find during a physical assessment of a female with Type I FGM?

options.A: The entire vaginal canal has been tightly stitched closed
options.B: Both the clitoris and both sets of labia are completely excised
options.C: Only the clitoris or its surrounding fold is partially or totally removed
options.D: Chemical burning or scraping of the tissue was performed

explanation: Correct! Type I focuses specifically on the clitoris and its hood without cutting away the labia. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h2)

question: A 16-year-old mother is getting ready for discharge after delivery. What is a top priority for her discharge education?

options.A: Information on filing for adult emancipation
options.B: Dietary guidelines for managing geriatric menopause
options.C: Instruction on how to return to competitive sports immediately
options.D: Contraception counseling to prevent rapid repeat pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Teenage mothers have a high chance of getting pregnant again too soon, so family planning guidance before discharge is vital. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the best way to communicate with a patient experiencing memory issues or confusion?

options.A: Use short, simple sentences and ask one question at a time
options.B: Ask multiple questions at once to save time
options.C: Avoid speaking to the patient and talk only to the wall
options.D: Argue with the patient whenever they become confused

explanation: Keep it brief and sweet! Asking too many things at once can easily overwhelm someone who is dealing with cognitive decline. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h4)

question: A young, single mother is struggling with depression, debt, and a crying baby with colic. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: The family has multiple overlapping risk factors for potential maltreatment
options.B: Depression in mothers has no proven link to child neglect
options.C: The infant is safe because colic is a temporary developmental stage
options.D: Financial debt is the sole driver of abuse in this household

explanation: Young age, mental stress, money troubles, and a fussy baby pile up to create high risk. This family needs extra support! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h3)

question: Why do night-shift nurses often find it hard to sleep during the day? Daytime light affects which hormone?

options.A: Aldosterone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Daylight tells your biological clock to keep melatonin levels low, which is why sleeping during the day after a night shift can be so tough. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h5)

question: What is the most common form of dementia seen among older adults?

options.A: Vascular dementia
options.B: Frontotemporal dementia
options.C: Lewy body dementia
options.D: Alzheimer's disease

explanation: You'll see this a lot in clinical practice! Alzheimer's disease accounts for the vast majority of all dementia cases worldwide. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h1)

question: What is the very first check a nurse must perform before giving any medication?

options.A: Check the expiration date on the medication packaging
options.B: Verify the patient's identity using two unique identifiers
options.C: Ask the doctor if the prescription is still valid
options.D: Measure the patient's current vital signs

explanation: Ensuring you have the correct person is the primary safeguard in healthcare before administering any treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a form of social stigma for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Receiving appropriate medical rehabilitation therapies
options.B: Encountering buildings with no wheelchair ramps
options.C: Being excluded from community social gatherings
options.D: Facing derogatory language and public staring

explanation: Spot on! Rehab therapy is supportive healthcare. Staring, lack of ramps, and exclusion are unfair barriers and forms of stigma. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h5)

question: What do we mean by 'happy hypoxemia' in COVID-19 care?

options.A: Feeling overly energetic despite severe viral fatigue and muscle aches
options.B: Experiencing extreme chest pain while maintaining normal oxygen levels
options.C: Showing high fever and cough while blood pressure remains stable
options.D: Having dangerously low blood oxygen without feeling short of breath

explanation: You got it! Some patients have shockingly low oxygen levels yet feel completely fine, which is why checking vital signs with a pulse oximeter is so important. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is patient safety in maternity care uniquely complex?

options.A: Pregnancy completely prevents any physical or medical complications
options.B: The nurse must monitor and protect two distinct lives at the same time
options.C: Labor and delivery wards never experience staffing shortages
options.D: Maternity patients never follow clinical instructions or take medications

explanation: In maternity care, you are caring for both the mother and the baby. That doubles your watch duty and your clinical responsibility! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which muscle acts as a gatekeeper, controlling the passage of food from the stomach into the small intestine?

options.A: Cardiac sphincter
options.B: Anal sphincter
options.C: Ileocecal valve
options.D: Pyloric sphincter

explanation: You've got this! The pyloric sphincter sits at the lower end of the stomach, acting like a tap to control when digested food moves into the small intestine. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h1)

question: What should the nurse do first before starting a physical examination?

options.A: Ask the family members to leave the hospital room
options.B: Prepare the environment and gather needed equipment
options.C: Perform a deep tissue palpation of the abdomen
options.D: Administer prescribed pain medications immediately

explanation: Organizing your tools and space beforehand prevents interruptions and keeps the patient calm and comfortable. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What essential instruction must be given about sexual partners when treating infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Partners can continue unprotected intercourse during the treatment week.
options.B: Partners only need treatment if they develop severe abdominal pain.
options.C: Only partners with visible symptoms need prescription medication.
options.D: Sexual partners must be checked and treated at the same time.

explanation: Treating partners together is the only way to stop the annoying ping-pong game of passing the infection back and forth! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h6)

question: What is the immediate next step after a school nurse identifies a health defect during a screening?

options.A: Providing a prompt referral for further clinical care
options.B: Keeping the finding secret from the parents
options.C: Prescribing specialized medicines immediately
options.D: Expelling the student from the school system

explanation: Screening is only useful if followed by a referral so the child can receive proper diagnosis and treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h7)

question: A hospital audit reveals that half of all postpartum women did not receive timely blood pressure checks. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Hide the report so the hospital management does not get angry
options.B: Share the feedback with the nurses and retrain staff on monitoring
options.C: Blame individual patients for refusing their vital signs checks
options.D: Stop taking blood pressures entirely to save nursing time

explanation: Audit results must be used to provide feedback and education to correct gaps in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the main role of the nurse when working as part of an interprofessional healthcare team?

options.A: Performing all physical and occupational therapy sessions alone
options.B: Handling only the financial and discharge paperwork for the hospital
options.C: Overriding decisions made by physicians and therapists
options.D: Acting as the central coordinator who synthesizes updates from all disciplines

explanation: Because you are at the bedside around the clock, you bring together updates from doctors, therapists, and dietitians to keep everyone on the same page! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h6)

question: What is the texture of a pureed diet?

options.A: Small, bite-sized pieces of tender meat
options.B: A smooth, pudding-like paste with no lumps
options.C: A mixture of solid chunks and thin liquids
options.D: Crispy foods that dissolve easily in the mouth

explanation: Pureed diets require zero chewing because all foods are blended completely smooth. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of using single-dose medication vials?

options.A: They let nurses reuse syringes safely
options.B: They make the medicine taste sweeter
options.C: They completely stop the risk of contaminating shared medicine bottles
options.D: They mean fewer patients will need shots

explanation: Single-dose vials are used once and thrown away. No sharing means no chance of passing germs into the next dose! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h7)

question: What happens when homeostatic failure is left untreated for too long?

options.A: Vital organs begin to shut down and shock can occur
options.B: The patient enters a state of deep relaxation
options.C: The body automatically fixes itself without any help
options.D: Blood pressure rises to a very safe level

explanation: Spot on. If the body's regulatory systems stay broken down, tissues are starved of oxygen, which can quickly lead to organ failure and shock. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is it dangerous to use traditional home remedies like forcing caustic liquids or oils down someone's throat after they swallow a poison?

options.A: Traditional remedies always cure toxic exposures faster than modern hospital drugs.
options.B: Community members refuse to visit hospitals unless accompanied by a nurse.
options.C: Practices like forcing caustic liquids or oils down the throat can worsen tissue injury and cause aspiration.
options.D: Myths prevent patients from paying their hospital bills on time.

explanation: Forcing things down can cause the chemical to burn the throat a second time on the way back up, or slip into the lungs and cause deadly pneumonia. Always educate gently against this! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h9)

question: What is the most frequent cause of blocked fallopian tubes leading to female infertility?

options.A: Congenital absence of the uterus
options.B: Excessive daily intake of dietary caffeine
options.C: Chronic low blood pressure

options.C: It reduces the total number of students in the classroom
options.D: It builds trust and encourages more parents to support projects

question: Unlike hospital nursing which looks after one patient at a time, what is the main focus of community health nursing?

options.A: The health of entire populations and communities
options.B: Critical care management in intensive units
options.C: Laboratory testing and biomedical research
options.D: Surgical interventions and post-operative recovery

explanation: Spot on! While hospital nurses care for individual bedside patients, community nurses look at the bigger picture—the health needs of whole neighborhoods and populations. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h1)

question: What kind of bowel sounds do you usually hear early on when a patient has a mechanical small bowel obstruction?

options.A: Completely absent sounds
options.B: Normal regular gurgles
options.C: Sustained swishing bruits
options.D: High-pitched, tinkling sounds

explanation: As the bowel strains to push contents past the tight spot, it creates those characteristic high-pitched, tinkling sounds right above the blockage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is a key nursing action when a dying patient is experiencing spiritual distress?

options.A: Ignore the comments because physical comfort is the only priority
options.B: Arrange a visit from a spiritual leader who matches the patient's beliefs
options.C: Convince the patient to adopt your own personal religious philosophy
options.D: Administer a sedative medication to calm the patient's anxious mind

explanation: Holistic care means caring for the spirit too. Connecting them with someone who shares their faith brings great peace. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the largest component of total daily energy expenditure for most people?

options.A: Planned athletic exercise
options.B: Basal or resting metabolic rate
options.C: Adaptive thermogenesis
options.D: Thermic effect of food

explanation: Keeping your internal organs alive and functioning at rest takes up the vast majority of the calories you burn daily. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h3)

question: Which hormone imbalance is a main trigger for most endometrial cancers?

options.A: Excess testosterone and low insulin
options.B: Deficiency in thyroid stimulating hormone
options.C: High levels of progesterone with low estrogen
options.D: Excess estrogen without enough progesterone

explanation: Spot on! When estrogen has no progesterone to balance it out, the uterine lining thickens too much, raising cancer risk. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h3)

question: What is drug antagonism in plain terms?

options.A: Two drugs combine to create a much larger therapeutic effect
options.B: Plasma protein binding sites become overloaded with free drug
options.C: One drug blocks or counteracts the effect of another drug
options.D: Liver enzymes speed up the clearance of both medications

explanation: Imagine two kids fighting over a single chair. Antagonism is when one drug jumps onto a cell receptor and blocks another substance from getting in or working! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h3)

question: A newly bereaved family member sits quietly without crying and says everything is fine. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The person is lying to trick the medical staff
options.B: The person lacks any emotional capacity for love
options.C: The person may be experiencing shock or emotional numbing
options.D: The person has already successfully reached full acceptance

explanation: A lack of tears does not always mean peace; it often indicates emotional shock or denial. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which category makes up the vast majority of all CJD cases?

options.A: Iatrogenic CJD
options.B: Variant CJD
options.C: Sporadic CJD
options.D: Familial CJD

explanation: Correct! Most CJD cases happen sporadically—meaning they appear out of nowhere for no known reason, without any inherited gene or infection link. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which protective layer of the meninges wraps directly and tightly around the surface of the spinal cord?

options.A: Pia mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteum
options.D: Dura mater

explanation: Great job! The pia mater is the innermost, delicate layer that hugs every single curve and groove of the spinal cord and brain like a second skin. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h2)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a child with marasmus and one with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Marasmus causes high fever and rashes, while kwashiorkor causes breathing failure
options.B: Children with kwashiorkor have no body fat loss at all compared to normal children
options.C: Kwashiorkor only affects teenagers, while marasmus only affects newborn infants
options.D: Marasmus children have severe muscle wasting and look very thin, while kwashiorkor children show pitting edema and swelling

explanation: Great job! Marasmus is like severe starvation with extreme thinness, while kwashiorkor features notable swelling (edema) from lack of protein. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h5)

question: Which white blood cells are mainly responsible for making antibodies?

options.A: B-lymphocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: You nailed it! B-lymphocytes are the antibody factories of your immune system, churning out proteins that target specific invaders. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason health leaders must set clear priorities in a community?

options.A: Resources like staff, money, and supplies are always limited
options.B: Health workers prefer doing easy tasks before hard ones
options.C: Government rules forbid spending money on more than one project
options.D: Communities demand that all diseases be treated on the same day

explanation: You got it! Because funds and supplies are never infinite, setting priorities helps us tackle what matters most first. Practical public health at its best! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h5)

question: What actually defines an ethical dilemma in nursing?

options.A: A situation where two or more moral principles conflict with each other
options.B: A disagreement between a nurse and a doctor over medication dosage
options.C: A patient refusing to pay their nursing agency bills
options.D: A broken piece of medical equipment inside the patient's home

explanation: Spot on! It's a tough spot where every choice seems to break a moral rule, and there is no easy right or wrong answer. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h8)

question: How can you tell the difference between the baby's side of the placenta and the mother's side?

options.A: The fetal surface contains the placental cotyledons, while the maternal surface has the umbilical cord insertion.
options.B: The fetal surface is smooth, shiny, and shows branching blood vessels, while the maternal surface is rough and divided into cotyledons.
options.C: The fetal surface is dark red and rough, while the maternal surface is covered by a clear, slippery amniotic membrane.
options.D: There is no visual difference between the two sides of a mature human placenta.

explanation: Picture it this way: the baby's side faces the shiny amniotic sac with visible blood vessels, while the mother's side faces the uterine wall and looks bumpy and rough. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h5)

question: A patient reports hot flashes, night sweats, and irregular cycles. Which body systems are these complaints linked to?

options.A: Endocrine and reproductive systems
options.B: Musculoskeletal system
options.C: Gastrointestinal system
options.D: Respiratory system

explanation: You've got this! Hot flashes and night sweats happen when estrogen levels shift, which ties directly back to our hormone (endocrine) and reproductive systems. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why must instrument packs inside an autoclave chamber be loosely arranged rather than tightly packed?

options.A: Loose packs dry much faster after the cycle ends
options.B: Tightly packed metal will melt from the intense heat
options.C: Air pockets help the machine reach high pressure quicker
options.D: Steam must circulate freely around every item

explanation: If packs are squeezed together, steam cannot penetrate the center, leaving some instruments unsterilized. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Which two hormones play the biggest role in helping uterine fibroids grow?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone fuel the growth of these muscle cells. That is why fibroids are so closely tied to a woman's reproductive years! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h2)

question: What do we mean by 'nutrient quantification' in nursing and nutrition?

options.A: The process of measuring exact amounts of nutrients in food or the body
options.B: The chemical breakdown of proteins in the stomach
options.C: The calculation of total daily fluid intake and output
options.D: The surgical removal of excess fat tissue from the abdomen

explanation: Think of nutrient quantification as measuring out the exact amounts of nutrients someone eats or needs. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h1)

question: Which sign is a classic clue of right-sided heart congestion?

options.A: Complete loss of vision in both eyes
options.B: Sudden wheezing and frothy pink sputum
options.C: Severe sharp chest pain radiating to the jaw
options.D: Peripheral edema and jugular venous distension

explanation: When the right side backs up, blood dams up in the body's veins. This leads to swollen ankles (edema) and bulging neck veins (jugular venous distension). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which group forms the backbone of direct healthcare delivery in Nigerian primary clinics?

options.A: International policy makers
options.B: Hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses and midwives
options.D: Pharmaceutical manufacturers

explanation: That's you! Nurses and midwives provide the vast majority of direct maternal and child health care across our communities. You are truly the heartbeat of healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why would a doctor order a 24-hour Holter monitor for a patient with occasional dizzy spells?

options.A: To continuously measure the oxygen saturation levels in the blood overnight
options.B: To deliver mild electrical shocks if the patient's heart rate drops too low
options.C: To catch intermittent dysrhythmias that do not happen during a quick clinic visit
options.D: To permanently replace the need for an invasive cardiac catheterization

explanation: Some heart flutters only happen once in a while. A 24-hour Holter monitor records the rhythm all day and night at home, helping catch those sneaky, unpredictable episodes! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should community members be involved in evaluating health projects?

options.A: It stops the government from auditing the facility
options.B: It gives them the legal right to close the clinic down
options.C: It is required only for international funding bodies
options.D: It promotes accountability and shows them the results of their work

explanation: Involving locals in evaluation builds transparency and lets them see how their participation improved community health. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)

question: What famous milestone did James Lind achieve when he tested citrus fruits on sailors?

options.A: The chemical isolation of pure vitamin C in a laboratory
options.B: The creation of the first national food pyramid
options.C: An early controlled clinical trial using citrus fruits for scurvy
options.D: The discovery of complex carbohydrates in grains

explanation: You nailed it! Lind compared different treatments and proved that oranges and lemons could cure sailors suffering from scurvy. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h3)

question: A hospital introduces a system that allows bedside nurses to help make decisions about clinical care standards. What concept does this show?

options.A: Rigid top-down command
options.B: Decentralisation and empowerment
options.C: High mechanistic control
options.D: Strict work specialisation

explanation: When bedside nurses get a voice in clinical decisions, power is shared downward. That is a great example of decentralisation and staff empowerment! [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h7)

question: When do we typically expect a secondary postpartum haemorrhage to happen?

options.A: During the immediate pushing of the placenta
options.B: Only after the baby stops breastfeeding completely
options.C: Within the first two hours after a CS
options.D: Between 24 hours and six weeks after delivery

explanation: Secondary PPH shows up later—anytime from 24 hours up to six weeks postpartum. It's usually caused by tiny bits of leftover tissue or an infection. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h1)

question: What surgical procedure is often necessary during childbirth for a woman with Type III FGM?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Oophorectomy
options.C: Cervical cerclage
options.D: Defibulation

explanation: Brilliant! Defibulation means carefully cutting open the scar tissue seal so the mother can have a safe delivery and examination. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h4)

question: What exactly is colostrum?

options.A: The thick, yellowish first breast milk produced after birth
options.B: The primary protein supplement used to treat severe malnutrition
options.C: A local porridge made from fermented yellow maize
options.D: A traditional herbal drink given to calm crying babies

explanation: Colostrum is the super-nutritious, antibody-rich milk that comes right after delivery. Sadly, bad taboos sometimes cause mothers to throw it away—good thing you know better! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h4)

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's vital signs before giving certain medications?

options.A: To update the hospital biometric database automatically
options.B: To determine how much the patient's hospital bill will increase
options.C: To fulfill a routine hospital requirement with no clinical value
options.D: To ensure the patient's current status makes the drug safe to give

explanation: Pre-administration assessment catches physiological changes, like low blood pressure or a slow heart rate, that make a scheduled drug unsafe. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding drug distribution?

options.A: Calculating the exact molecular weight of every pill
options.B: Surgically placing IV lines directly into brain tissue
options.C: Synthesizing new chemical formulas in the ward
options.D: Monitoring for unexpected side effects from altered drug binding or blood flow

explanation: As a nurse, you are the safety net! Watching how your patient responds and checking their labs helps you catch any drug distribution issues early on. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h8)

question: What does a holistic evaluation of a palliative patient include?

options.A: Surgical history and previous childhood illnesses only
options.B: Only laboratory test results and vital sign trends
options.C: Physical, psychological, social, and spiritual well-being
options.D: Financial statements and insurance coverage limits

explanation: Holistic care addresses every aspect of a person's life, recognizing that emotional and spiritual pain affects physical comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h2)

question: Which animal is the main reservoir responsible for spreading the Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Stray cats
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Pigs and swine
options.D: Multimammate rats

question: At what heart rate should you start chest compressions during newborn resuscitation?

options.A: Below 60 beats per minute
options.B: Below 80 beats per minute
options.C: Below 40 beats per minute
options.D: Below 100 beats per minute

question: A hormone travels through the whole body, but why does it only affect certain cells?

options.A: Non-target cells actively destroy the hormone on contact

options.C: Target cells are the only ones physically close to endocrine glands
options.D: Target cells possess specific receptors that bind to that hormone

question: Why would an occupational health nurse schedule regular hearing (audiometric) tests for factory workers?

options.A: To evaluate stress from night shift rotations
options.B: To detect early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it becomes permanent
options.C: To measure lung capacity after chemical dust exposure
options.D: To screen for bloodborne infections from shared gear

explanation: Spot on! Regular hearing tests help catch any hearing damage early on, before it turns into permanent deafness. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h5)

question: A patient with severe knee osteoarthritis gets no relief from oral pain relievers and physical therapy. What intervention is a nurse most likely to prepare the patient for next?

options.A: A complete blood transfusion
options.B: An intraarticular joint injection
options.C: Intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.D: An intramuscular vaccine dose

explanation: When conservative oral treatments fail for localized joint wear, doctors often step up to direct joint injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: How do clinic registers help nurses identify children who have defaulted?

options.A: By calculating the exact weight the child will gain next month
options.B: By predicting which family will move to another state
options.C: By automatically ordering new vaccine vials from the depot
options.D: By tracking missed return dates between scheduled clinic visits

explanation: Facility registers record attendance dates, making it easy to see when a child fails to return for their next scheduled dose. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: What does 'hidden hunger' refer to in public health?

options.A: A temporary shortage of food caused by hidden transport strikes
options.B: A secret eating disorder common among teenagers in urban centers
options.C: A lack of essential micronutrients despite consuming enough daily calories
options.D: The physical sensation of hunger experienced only during night shifts

explanation: Hidden hunger happens when diets fill the stomach with cheap energy sources but lack vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)

question: What should you warn your patient about right before you start a bladder irrigation?

options.A: Immediate drowsiness and heavy sleepiness
options.B: A strong urge to urinate or mild cramping
options.C: Numbness spreading down both upper legs
options.D: A sharp burning sensation in the lower back

explanation: No need to alarm them—just let them know that filling the bladder naturally tricks the body into feeling like it really needs to pee! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h4)

question: Which viral STI is managed with lifelong antivirals to keep painful blisters under control?

options.A: Herpes Simplex Virus
options.B: Cytomegalovirus
options.C: Human Papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis A Virus

explanation: Herpes simplex causes flare-ups of painful blisters. Antivirals don't cure the virus completely, but they help manage and shorten the outbreaks. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: What major change happens to the spine in advanced ankylosing spondylitis?

options.A: Cartilage between discs completely dissolves and leaks
options.B: Vertebrae fuse together into a rigid structure
options.C: Spinal nerves swell and permanently pinch the spinal cord
options.D: Bones become overly soft and prone to micro-fractures

question: What is the main job of the ductus arteriosus?

question: What are the three classic actions that make NSAIDs a go-to drug class in clinical practice?

options.A: Muscle relaxation, sedation, and blood thinning
options.B: Blood pressure reduction, diuresis, and infection cure
options.C: Bronchodilation, mucus clearance, and cough suppression
options.D: Pain relief, fever reduction, and anti-inflammation

explanation: Remember the big three for NSAIDs: analgesics (pain), antipyretics (fever), and anti-inflammatories (swelling). You'll see these used everywhere on the ward! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is teaching children not to share personal items so important in schools?

options.A: Teachers are legally required to diagnose skin conditions during morning assembly
options.B: Children frequently exchange items like combs and caps, spreading fungal and parasitic infections
options.C: Sharing clothes is the only known method of bacterial transmission
options.D: Schools lack the budget to buy chemical disinfectants for classroom desks

explanation: Kids love sharing caps and combs, which unfortunately makes it super easy to pass around things like lice and ringworm! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h8)

question: What is a common reason why people strictly follow food taboos?

options.A: Direct orders from national medical boards
options.B: Lack of physical transport to farms
options.C: High market prices for the forbidden foods
options.D: Fear of social disapproval, curses, or bad luck

explanation: Taboos are tied to deep spiritual beliefs, so people worry about negative social or supernatural consequences if they break the rules. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h2)

question: Why is it important for researchers to discuss study limitations during data interpretation?

options.A: To prove that their research is completely flawless and superior
options.B: To justify increasing the budget for future research projects
options.C: To confuse readers so they do not question the findings
options.D: To honestly acknowledge any weaknesses or factors that could affect the results

explanation: No study is perfect, and transparency about limitations builds scientific credibility. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the purpose of the 'teach-back' method in home care?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to grade the family's cleaning skills
options.B: Checking if the patient or caregiver truly understands instructions
options.C: Testing the patient's ability to read a textbook out loud
options.D: Teaching the nurse how to use home appliances

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?', you ask them to explain the instructions back to you in their own words. It's a game-changer for safety! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h8)

question: Your patient just woke up from surgery and feels dizzy. What should you do about getting them out of bed?

options.A: Use a standard sliding board without help
options.B: Ask the patient to walk alone to test their strength
options.C: Lift the patient quickly to avoid bedsores
options.D: Postpone the transfer and reassess the dizziness

explanation: Dizziness is a warning sign of weakness or low blood pressure. It's always safer to let them rest until they are steady. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.B: To replace hospital chemotherapy entirely
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve suffering
options.D: To completely cure aggressive tumors

explanation: Palliative care is all about comfort, dignity, and making sure patients and their families feel supported when a cure isn't possible. Beautiful, compassionate nursing! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h8)

question: What does it mean if a patient has a congenital absence of a fallopian tube?

options.A: The tube was blocked by scar tissue from endometriosis
options.B: The tube failed to form during embryonic development
options.C: The tube was surgically removed due to infection
options.D: The tube was destroyed by a ruptured ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! 'Congenital' simply means present from birth, meaning the tube never developed in the first place. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h3)

question: Why do patients with advanced HIV catch unusual bugs like Pneumocystis pneumonia?

options.A: Their weakened immune systems cannot fight off normal environmental organisms.
options.B: The virus directly mutates lung tissue into cancerous cells.
options.C: Antiretroviral drugs cause severe respiratory tract paralysis.
options.D: Red blood cells lose their ability to carry oxygen to the lungs.

explanation: These are called opportunistic infections—they take advantage of a weak immune system to cause sickness. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h5)

question: In community health nursing, what do we mean by a "food taboo"?

options.A: A cultural rule against eating certain foods
options.B: A government law controlling food prices
options.C: A medical prescription for weight loss
options.D: An allergic reaction to specific meals

explanation: A food taboo is simply a cultural or religious rule that says 'no' to eating certain edible items. You'll see this often in community postings! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h1)

question: Which client is most at risk for having a very hard time adjusting after losing a spouse?

options.A: A client who anticipated the death for many years following a chronic illness

options.C: A client who participates actively in a supportive religious community
options.D: A client who has successfully coped with multiple past life crises

explanation: Spot on! When someone relies completely on their partner and lacks a strong backup support system, the loss hits much harder and recovery is tougher. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is a major risk if a patient goes home without proper family training and home preparation?

options.A: Immediate complete recovery of motor function
options.B: Lower levels of caregiver stress
options.C: Decreased need for community follow-up care
options.D: High rates of preventable rehospitalization

question: Where does a primary health clinic in Nigeria send its monthly injection safety report first?

options.A: The Local Government Area (LGA) focal officer
options.B: The international donor agency headquarters
options.C: The nearest private pharmaceutical distributor
options.D: Directly to the Federal Minister of Health

question: What part of a parasitic egg helps it survive harsh outside conditions?

options.A: The tough outer shell
options.B: The internal moving larva
options.C: The flagella tails
options.D: The watery cytoplasm

explanation: That multi-layered outer shell acts like armor, protecting the egg from drying out and handling environmental hazards. Well done! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which two major organs take the heaviest hit from long-term, uncontrolled high blood pressure?

options.A: Liver and pancreas
options.B: Heart and kidneys
options.C: Lungs and stomach
options.D: Spleen and thyroid

explanation: Because the heart and kidneys are packed with delicate blood vessels, they bear the brunt of constant high pressure, leading to heart and kidney failure over time. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h8)

question: What is the main job of the fluid inside serous membranes?

options.A: To supply oxygen directly to outer tissue layers
options.B: To regulate the internal temperature of abdominal organs
options.C: To reduce friction between moving organs and cavity walls
options.D: To trap invading bacteria and fight localized infections

question: Where do you usually find the cell bodies of most sensory neurons?

options.A: Skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Dorsal root ganglia
options.C: Motor cortex of the brain
options.D: Anterior horns of the spinal cord

question: What key instruction should you give a patient about how much topical cream to use?

options.A: Mix all prescribed creams together to save time
options.B: Use only the exact prescribed amount in a thin layer
options.C: Stop applying the cream the moment the redness fades slightly
options.D: Apply as much as possible so it cures the condition faster

explanation: More isn't always better! Piling on extra cream doesn't speed up healing; it just increases the risk of skin irritation and unwanted side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h9)

question: You are caring for an unconscious patient with a severe brain injury. Which nursing action best prevents aspiration?

options.A: Removing all oral secretions using a tongue blade
options.B: Laying the patient flat on their back to rest
options.C: Keeping the head of the bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: Feeding small pureed meals every two hours

explanation: Gravity is your friend here! Elevating the bed stops stomach contents and saliva from flowing back into the lungs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h5)

question: What should a nurse do if a sterile instrument pack has a torn or damp wrapper?

options.A: Discard or return the item because sterility is lost
options.B: Wipe the outside with alcohol and place it back on the shelf
options.C: Use it quickly before any dust can settle inside
options.D: Ask another nurse to approve using it for a minor dressing

explanation: Any damage or moisture to a sterile wrapper compromises the barrier, meaning the instruments are no longer safe to use. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: What happens during codominance?

options.A: Mutations destroy both alleles before birth
options.B: The physical traits from both parents blend together completely
options.C: Both alleles are expressed equally and independently
options.D: One dominant allele completely hides the recessive allele

explanation: In codominance, neither allele masks the other; both are fully visible in the organism, such as in AB blood groups. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of palliative care when dealing with advanced breast cancer?

options.A: To train the patient to perform clinical breast exams on others
options.B: To reverse the side effects of prior chemotherapy drugs
options.C: To improve quality of life and relieve distressing symptoms
options.D: To completely cure the metastatic cancer cells in the bones

explanation: When a cure isn't possible anymore, palliative care steps in to wrap the patient in comfort, pain relief, and dignity. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h8)

question: What is the primary change in lung tissue for a patient with pulmonary fibrosis?

options.A: Accumulation of watery transudate in the pleural cavity
options.B: Dilation and destruction of the small alveolar air sacs
options.C: Hypersecretion of thick mucus in the large main bronchi
options.D: Replacement of normal lung tissue with stiff scar tissue

explanation: Brilliant! Pulmonary fibrosis is all about chronic inflammation turning healthy lung tissue into stiff, non-stretchy scar tissue. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h5)

question: What might happen if a poor metabolizer takes a prodrug that relies on enzymes to become active?

options.A: The drug may fail to produce the desired therapeutic effect
options.B: The drug converts instantly and causes severe acute toxicity
options.C: The liver permanently stores the drug in fatty tissues
options.D: The kidneys immediately flush the drug out unchanged

explanation: That's right! Prodrugs need liver enzymes to wake them up and make them active. If those enzymes are too slow, the drug won't work like it should. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why might a patient with chronic pain need a higher dose of their pain medication after taking it for several months?

options.A: Receptor desensitization causes drug tolerance
options.B: Kidney filtration rate slows down with age
options.C: Gastrointestinal absorption becomes blocked
options.D: The liver begins storing the drug in fatty tissue

explanation: After months of constant stimulation, the cell receptors get tired and stop responding as much. That's tolerance in action! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h7)

question: A conscious patient with terminal cancer firmly refuses a blood transfusion because of personal beliefs. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Administer the blood anyway because it is life-saving
options.B: Ask the family to force the patient to accept the treatment
options.C: Wait until the patient falls asleep and give the transfusion
options.D: Respect the refusal and notify the healthcare team

explanation: Even if treatment can save a life, a competent adult has the legal and ethical right to refuse it. Always honor your patient's autonomy and inform the team! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h3)

question: When is a nebulizer most commonly chosen over a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: When the patient needs a device that fits easily in a small shirt pocket
options.B: When treatment must be completed in less than five seconds
options.C: When the patient cannot coordinate deep breathing with a handheld inhaler
options.D: When the healthcare provider wants to avoid using any electricity or gas

explanation: Nebulizers produce a continuous mist over several minutes, making them great for young children, the elderly, or acutely breathless patients. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: A nurse hands a patient their morning pills, but the patient is busy talking on the phone and asks the nurse to leave the cup on the bedside table. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Place the pills in the patient's water cup so they dissolve for later
options.B: Take the pills away and document that the patient refused the medication
options.C: Leave the pills on the table and remind the nurse's assistant to check later
options.D: Stay with the patient, wait until they finish the call, and watch them take the pills

explanation: Medications should never be left unattended at the bedside because the patient might forget them, take them incorrectly, or someone else might take them. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of antimicrobial stewardship programs in hospitals?

options.A: To ensure all patients receive broad-spectrum coverage daily
options.B: To eliminate the need for bacterial laboratory cultures
options.C: To promote the correct and careful use of antibacterial drugs
options.D: To find cheaper generic substitutes for every medication

explanation: Stewardship is all about making sure antibiotics are used wisely so they don't lose their power over time. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h5)
